summary.plain: A roughly 10-metre cube of instruments at LEP's Point 8, famous for being able to tell exactly which kind of charged particle flew through it using rings of light (Cherenkov radiation).
summary.technical: General-purpose LEP detector, about 10 m in length and diameter, with roughly 20 subdetectors: a Ring Imaging Cherenkov (RICH) system for full charged-particle identification and a high-precision silicon vertex detector for short-lived-particle tracking, alongside standard tracking, calorimetry and muon systems.

technology.quote: The DELPHI detector used the ring imaging Cherenkov technique to differentiate between secondary charged particles
technology.value: General-purpose collider detector with Ring Imaging Cherenkov particle identification and precision silicon vertexing
